text:
Anna (PM): Quick sync 1: drafting a one-page launch checklist for Private deployments where the customer runs networking. Need minimal operational guarantees + clear caller responsibilities.

Raj (Eng): +1. My take: installer must support non-destructive rolling upgrades, documented IP mapping, fast preflight failures, and an optional fallback to hosted control-plane for telemetry only.

Marta (Field): Customers repeatedly ask for 'no IP churn' and a supported rollback path. We also need to be explicit about what field will assist vs what the customer must own during cutover.

Kyle (NetOps): From netops: we need an egress IP verification step, a BGP handoff dry-run, and the installer to emit final egress mapping. If we promise IP preservation, we must validate it with a test harness.

Jia (SRE): Observability needs: minimal upgrade-health metrics, an event trace that maps to operator actions, and telemetry toggles that respect customer KMS/policy. Also short runbook for common failures.

Raj (Eng): Draft acceptance gates (compact):
- Preflight: network reachability, required ports, disk and kernel versions, iptables/no conflicting NAT rules, ip mapping verified
- Upgrade: rolling agent upgrade with canary (configurable 10% -> 100%), atomic agent rollback support
- IP continuity: documented plan + signed test plan (customer network owner)
- Packaging: online installer + airgap bundle (sha256-signed)
- Observability: health metrics + event log; telemetry opt-out and KMS-aware
- Support: contracted cutover assistance window + P1 triage SLA
- Exclusions: customer BGP misconfig, in-rack HW failures, unsupported kernel patches

Anna (PM): Can we convert that into a one-pager for field and sales? Keep bullets short and add a "customer responsibilities" column. Also explicitly state what we will not own.

Marta (Field): Yes. I9ll fill customer responsibilities: BGP prep, ASN/IP allocation, firewall changes, DNS cutover window, and an assigned network owner contact. Also include an FAQ with prior deal snafus.

Kyle (NetOps): Add gating test: a dry-run that simulates BGP handoff and verifies egress IP continuity. This must be executed and signed off before final cutover.

Jia (SRE): I9ll produce the minimal metrics list (CPU, mem, kube-probe, upgrade-progress-percent, egress-ip-diff) and a troubleshooting playbook for top 5 failure modes.

Raj (Eng): I9ll own the preflight script and rollback runbook. ETA Tue EOD.

Kyle (NetOps): I9ll provide the BGP handoff checklist and dry-run script. ETA Tue EOD.

Marta (Field): Drafting customer responsibilities + FAQ. ETA Wed AM.

Jia (SRE): Telemetry docs + runbook. ETA Wed noon.

Anna (PM): Final: do we gate GA on customer-verified cutovers? I propose require two successful cutovers on distinct topologies (one on-prem BGP, one cloud VPC) with rollback exercised.

Marta (Field): Strong yes. In prior launches, one successful customer test is not enough to catch edge cases. Require at least two.

Raj (Eng): Fine with that. Definition of success: upgrade + rollback executed, metrics stable, no IP drift, and post-cutover support window closed with no pending network defects.

Kyle (NetOps): Also require one of the verifications to be airgap or airgap-like.

Anna (PM): Great. I9ll assemble the one-page and internal checklist and ping for signoff. Thanks all. :pray:

deploy-bot: New doc uploaded: /docs/private-deploy/launch-gates-v1.md (internal)

Marta (Field): noted, will review once Anna posts the draft. :eyes:
